info.name: E-Shop API
info.description:
Full API collection for the E-Shop Spring Boot backend, generated from the active controllers in src/main/java/com/example/learning_spring_security/controller.

Auth: most admin endpoints require a Bearer JWT with ADMIN role/authority. Log in via the 'Auth' folder first, then set the {{accessToken}} collection variable (or add a small script to the Login request's Tests tab: pm.collectionVariables.set('accessToken', pm.response.json().accessToken)).

Permission enforcement: @RequirePermission/PermissionAspect has been removed entirely. Every non-public request now goes through ApiPermissionInterceptor, which resolves the required funcId at runtime from an api_permissions row (method + URL pattern), then checks it against user_permissions for the calling user. This is fail-closed: any authenticated endpoint with no matching api_permissions row returns 403 'API not configured for permission check', not open access. IMPORTANT: any user with the ADMIN authority - including the seeded 'admin' account this collection's Login request uses - bypasses this check entirely and can hit every endpoint in this collection regardless of api_permissions/user_permissions state. To actually exercise the fail-closed 403 behavior (Return/Cancelation folders, or any newly wired endpoint), log in as a non-admin user instead. See API_TESTING_GUIDE.md and PERMISSION_SYSTEM_GUIDE.md for the full flow and how to wire up a new endpoint. Function Permission / Group Permission / User Permission / User Group folders manage the funcId/user_permissions data itself, not the interceptor. Return (Admin) and Cancelation (Admin) folders are known-unwired endpoints - they have no api_permissions rows yet, so non-admin requests to those two folders return 403 until that's added.

Bakong / Bakong Webhook folders: BakongController is the app's own client-facing QR/status endpoints. BakongWebhookController is the intended Bakong-server-to-app callback, but it has no signature verification and requires authentication that an external Bakong server can't provide - treat it as a stub, not production-ready. Bakong itself may also reject calls entirely when this app is deployed on a host (e.g. Render's free tier) whose outbound IP isn't registered with NBC/Bakong.
